title: The Vijayanagara Empire
subtitle: The great south Indian empire of Hampi · 1336 – 1646
subject: vijayanagara-empire
intro: Founded on the Tungabhadra in the 14th century by the Sangama brothers, Vijayanagara grew into the dominant power of south India for over two centuries. Its capital at Hampi astonished Persian and European visitors; its kings patronised Telugu, Kannada, Sanskrit and Tamil literature and music; and its long rivalry with the Bahmani and Deccan sultanates shaped the Deccan. After the defeat at Talikota in 1565 the capital was abandoned, and the empire slowly broke up into the Nayak kingdoms and Mysore.

events.title: Founding by Harihara and Bukka
events.summary: The brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama family found a kingdom on the Tungabhadra after the Delhi Sultanate's raids into the south. Tradition credits the sage Vidyaranya of Sringeri as their guide and gives 18 April 1336 as the founding date; historians still debate the brothers' origins.

events.title: Hoysala lands absorbed
events.summary: After the death of the last major Hoysala king, the Sangama brothers take over the Hoysala territories, making Vijayanagara the main Hindu power south of the Krishna.

events.title: Bahmani Sultanate founded
events.summary: Rebel officers of the Delhi Sultanate found the Bahmani Sultanate in the northern Deccan, with its capital at Gulbarga (later Bidar). Wars between the two over the fertile Raichur Doab between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers recur for two centuries.

events.title: Conquest of the Madurai Sultanate
events.summary: Bukka's son Kumara Kampana conquers the Madurai Sultanate in the Tamil country. His wife Gangadevi celebrates the campaign in the Sanskrit poem Madhura Vijayam.

events.title: Harihara II takes the imperial title
events.summary: Under Bukka's son Harihara II, the Sangama rulers style themselves emperors and control most of south India.

events.title: Niccolò de' Conti visits
events.summary: The Venetian merchant Niccolò de' Conti describes a great city sixty miles around, with tens of thousands of men under arms.

events.title: Deva Raya II
events.summary: The high point of the Sangama dynasty. Deva Raya II recruits Muslim archers and cavalry into his army, campaigns as far as Sri Lanka's tributaries, and patronises Kannada and Telugu poets.

events.title: Abdur Razzaq's account
events.summary: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq visits the court of Deva Raya II and writes that 'the eye has seen nothing like it' — describing seven concentric walls, bazaars and the Mahanavami festival.

events.title: Saluva Narasimha seizes the throne
events.summary: With the Sangama line weakened and Gajapati armies from Odisha pressing south, the general Saluva Narasimha takes power — the first of the empire's usurpations.

events.title: The Bahmani Sultanate breaks up
events.summary: The Bahmani kingdom splits into five Deccan sultanates — Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar and Berar. Their rivalries let Vijayanagara play one against another.

events.title: Tuluva dynasty
events.summary: The Tuluva family, commanders under the Saluvas, take the throne in turn.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya crowned
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya begins a twenty-year reign usually seen as the empire's golden age, in military power, architecture and literature alike.

events.title: Building the capital
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya adds gopurams and halls to the Virupaksha Temple, builds the Krishna and Hazara Rama temples and begins the great Vittala temple; he also endows the Tirumala temple, where his statue still stands.

events.title: The Portuguese take Goa
events.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque captures Goa from Bijapur. The Portuguese become Vijayanagara's partners in the horse trade — warhorses from Arabia and Persia, essential for its cavalry.

events.title: Campaigns against the Gajapatis
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya takes the Gajapati strongholds of Udayagiri (1513) and Kondaveedu (1515) and pushes into coastal Andhra. The war ends with a treaty and his marriage to a Gajapati princess.

events.title: Domingo Paes in Vijayanagara
events.summary: The Portuguese visitor Domingo Paes describes the capital as 'as large as Rome' and gives a vivid portrait of Krishnadevaraya. Fernão Nunes adds a chronicle of the kings a decade later.

events.title: Amuktamalyada and the Ashtadiggajas
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya writes the Telugu poem Amuktamalyada, which includes advice on kingship. His court is remembered for eight great Telugu poets, the Ashtadiggajas, led by Allasani Peddana — and for the jester-poet Tenali Rama of popular stories.

events.title: Battle of Raichur
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya defeats Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur and takes the fortress of Raichur, winning control of the long-disputed Doab.

events.title: Purandara Dasa and Carnatic music
events.summary: The saint-composer Purandara Dasa, a disciple of Vyasatirtha who was the royal guru, lays down the teaching method of Carnatic music while living in Hampi.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya dies; Achyuta Raya succeeds
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya is succeeded by his half-brother Achyuta Deva Raya, whose reign is troubled by rivalry with the king's powerful son-in-law, Rama Raya.

events.title: Rama Raya takes control
events.summary: Sadasiva Raya is placed on the throne but kept as a figurehead. Rama Raya rules in his name and intervenes skilfully — and later, arrogantly — in the quarrels of the Deccan sultans.

events.title: Tirumala moves to Penukonda; Aravidu dynasty
events.summary: Rama Raya's brother Tirumala Deva Raya escapes with the treasury and the puppet king, makes Penukonda his capital and founds the Aravidu dynasty.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar unite against Vijayanagara. At the battle near Talikota (Rakkasa-Tangadi) the Vijayanagara army breaks after two of its Muslim commanders reportedly change sides; Rama Raya is captured and beheaded.

events.title: Hampi sacked and abandoned
events.summary: The victorious armies plunder the undefended capital for months. Vijayanagara city is never reoccupied; its ruins at Hampi are today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: Revival under Venkatapati Raya
events.summary: Venkatapati Raya restores much of the empire's authority, moves the capital to Chandragiri, and resists Golconda.

events.title: Mysore's Wodeyars take Srirangapatna
events.summary: Raja Wodeyar takes Srirangapatna from the Vijayanagara viceroy — the start of the independent Kingdom of Mysore, later ruled by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.

events.title: Battle of Toppur — civil war
events.summary: A succession dispute after Venkatapati's death leads to a ruinous civil war. The Nayaks of Madurai and Thanjavur, nominally governors, act more and more independently.

events.title: Madras granted to the English
events.summary: Under the authority of the Vijayanagara emperor Venkata III, a local Nayaka grants Francis Day of the East India Company a strip of coast, where Fort St. George and the city of Madras (Chennai) grow.

events.title: Shahaji in the former Vijayanagara lands
events.summary: Bijapur's conquests in the old Vijayanagara south are led partly by Shahaji Bhosale, Shivaji's father, who holds Bangalore as his base.

events.title: End of the empire
events.summary: Sriranga III, the last emperor, loses his remaining territory to Bijapur and Golconda and to his own Nayaks; he dies in exile. The successor states — Mysore, Madurai, Thanjavur, Keladi — carry on Vijayanagara's traditions.

events.title: Marathas in Thanjavur
events.summary: Shivaji's half-brother Ekoji (Venkoji) replaces the Nayaks of Thanjavur, beginning a Maratha dynasty there that lasts until 1855.
